w: Today Paramswarup Swami brought a devotee for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Introducing him, he said, "Swami! This is Becharbhai, from Rohishala."
Swamishri kept looking at him. Searching his memory, he asked, "Which village were you in earlier?"
Paramswarup Swami said, "In Rohishala itself."
Swamishri was not satisfied, so Becharbhai, who had moved on ahead, was called back. He was asked, "Where did you live earlier?"
"Chakampar. I lived there for fifteen years."

A sparkle came into Swamishri's eyes. He immediately said, "Hmm... he had me visit his home twice in Chakampar. We used to stay with him a lot." Saying this, he squeezed Becharbhai's hand enthusiastically. After coming out, Paramswarup Swami asked Becharbhai, "When did you have Swamishri visit your home?"
"About forty or forty-five years ago." Once the house of memories of devotees is built in Swamishri's heart, it never breaks, nor does the dust of time settle on it.

Swamishri celebrated the 3rd Anniversary of the mandir inauguration (Patotsav) according to Vedic rites. Swamishri bathed the murtis with water, milk, curd, ghee and saffron.

In the evening assembly the small murti of Lord Harikrishna Maharaj (Thakorji) was brought ceremoniously in a palanquin and placed in a decorated seat. The murti of Harikrishna Maharaj was then honored.

Swamishri's 62nd Bhagwati diksha anniversary was celebrated. Swamishri offered puja and a garland to a murti of Shastriji Maharaj placed before Thakorji in the mandir. Amidst the diksha mantra sung by sadhus, Swamishri placed a janoi and tied a holy thread to the wrist of Shastriji Maharaj's murti. The morning assembly at 11.00 am celebrated the 62nd diksha anniversary. Bhajans and speeches by sadhus reflected the glory and saintliness of Swamishri. Haka Khachar spoke about Swamishri's greatness and the blessings showered upon Swamishri by Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.
Before puja, Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha ceremony for the murtis to be installed in the mandir at Lotava and Un, in the district of Surat.

On 26 December 2002, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was having breakfast in Atladra. At that time Sarvamangal Swami introduced Dineshbhai J. Patel, a satsangi devotee originally from Adas and living in London, saying, "He is the grandson of Madhabhai of Koyli, through his daughter."
Viveksagar Swami said, "Swami Bapa will give a fuller introduction."

Swamishri said, "Madhabhai had two brothers, Ishwarbhai and Naranbhai. Their father was Jijibhai Naranbhai. He became a sadhu in the time of Shastriji Maharaj. They all lived in Koyli. Their native village was Koyli. They invited Shastriji Maharaj, took him in procession on an elephant and welcomed him with music. Then Madhabhai stayed in Koyli itself. His sons, Govindbhai and the others, also stayed there, and Ishwarbhai kept land in Jesangpura, lived there and passed away to Akshardham there. He had two sons: Purushottambhai, who still comes here now, and the other, Chaturbhai. Chaturbhai had no children. Then Naranbhai had three sons: Lallubhai, Girdharbhai and Narsinhbhai. All three are maternal uncles of Devcharan Swami. Narsinhbhai came to become a sadhu. He also stayed with me. Then he went home. He too has young children. All of them had firm faith in Shastriji Maharaj. The families of all three brothers had firm faith."

When Swamishri gave this introduction, everyone was astounded. This darshan of Swamishri, woven into the lives of the devotees with an affection greater even than that of their own relatives, was something quite unique.

Shri Vishnubhai Bhatt built the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir as a top floor of his bungalow. Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha ceremony of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Radha Krishna Dev, Shri Tirupati Balaji, Shri Hanumanji, Shri Ganapatiji and Guru Parampara. After performing pujan and arti of the murtis, Swamishri addressed the assembly, “Sometimes you think that if you go to mandir then what will happen to my business? But God worries about that. Because when you come for darshan God feels, that since he has come to Me, I must look after him. God takes care of your business, job or farm and everything. God has taken care of the social responsibilities of His great devotees.”
Mandir is the root means to maintain one's dharma, culture and values. (21-12-2003, Chennai)
Our cultural values and bhakti are fostered through performing of worship of God's murti. (21-12-2003, Chennai)
We attain the virtues of satya, daya, ahimsa and brahmcharya by going to mandirs, reading of scriptures and spiritual association of sadhus. (21-12-2003, Chennai)
Dharma is our beauty, God is our life. ( 22-12-2003, Chennai)
A person desiring to serve our society, religion or country should first have pure character. (22-12-2003, Chennai)

Every month more than 6,000 to 7,000 devotees assemble from neighboring villages for the Punam assembly at the Sankari mandir. Today in the presence of Swamishri 14,000 devotees were present in the morning Punam assembly. Swamishri in his blessings to the assembly, said, "Today is Punam. Here you get the opportunity to do Thakorji's darshan and listen to discourses. Both, darshan and discourses, are eternal. The material happiness is temporary. Because one has not realized this one runs after that happiness and expends one's entire life... Bhagwan Swaminarayan has said that the essence of the four Vedas, six shastras, 18 Purans, Mahabharat and other scriptures is that God and His Sadhu are the means to moksha. We have all not read the shastras but the heart of what is preached is that we should give up this world and endeavor for moksha..."

Swamishri arrived at the Yogi Sabhagruh (hall in mandir) for the evening satsang assembly. Since it was the last Sunday of the year, a video depicting Swamishri’s annual achievements was shown in the assembly. In all, Swamishri had accomplished 42 projects, ranging from social, educational to spiritual. Pujya Viveksagar elaborated upon Swamishri’s 2010 vicharan in his discourse. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the assembly. He spoke about having profound faith in God, the service of Bhagatji Maharaj, the steadfastness of Maharaj’s paramhansas in spite of insult and persecution, and understanding the glory of God and his devotees.
The simplest way to moksha

19 December 2010, Mumbai Nimish Thakkar, a devotee, asked Swamishri by phone, “What should I do to attain moksha?” Swamishri replied briefly, “Have refuge in God. Do bhajan and bhakti, and observe moral disciplines; you will get moksha. Also, never doubt God’s doership.”
Priority in life

20 December 2010, Mumbai Swamishri is profoundly wedded to spirituality. Despite all his activities, doing bhajan is an intrinsic part of his persona. This morning Swamishri finished his bathing rituals earlier than usual. Since he was before time the attendant sadhus requested him to rest for a while. In response Swamishri replied, “It’s better to do bhajan than to lie down.” Swamishri turned the mala, chanting the Swaminarayan mantra, for 25 minutes.
Blessing a lost soul

22 December 2010, Mumbai A devotee from America explained on the phone, “Swamishri, my son (Yogi) used to regularly do his puja and observe the satsang disciplines. But since the last one-and-a-half years he has stopped doing puja. His mother has explained to Yogi to start again, and he did his puja today.” “Give him the phone,” Swamishri requested. Yogi came on the phone and Swamishri lovingly explained, “You are virtuous since childhood. You used to do puja before. And now that you have started, do it properly. Good sense has prevailed over you because of your devotion. I bless you for treading the right path and for inner strength and peace in life.”
Guru is the root of progress

23 December 2010, Mumbai Whenever Swamishri is praised for all his works and achievements he credits everything to his gurus Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. His appreciation rises from the wellspring of his guru bhakti. Adarshjivan Swami informed Swamishri, “Sant Swami (a senior sadhu) used to say that you have accomplished ten times more than what Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj had done.” “The wish [for all projects] was ultimately theirs, because they dreamed for more mandirs and an increase in Satsang. This is why such works are accomplished.” “Yes, they willed, but to make efforts in realizing their wishes is of no lesser importance,” Adarshjivan Swami added. Swamishri replied, “It was their wish, and that’s why things get done. There is power in their wishes.” Adarshjivan Swami stated, “In spite of the potential power in a seed, one needs someone to nourish it with water and nutrients. Only then will it flourish into a tree.” Swamishri argued, “But when the seed is genuine, then only the nutrients and water will lead to fruition.” Then Adarshjivan Swami rattled off an inventory of Swamishri’s 42 accomplishments in the year 2010. Swamishri answered, “Ultimately, the roots of all these achievements lie in the wishes of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. They wished for the increase in numbers of sadhus and the growth of Satsang. Yogiji Maharaj chanted dhun in the Akshar Deri for the growth of Satsang and in the number of sadhus. And that is why we see the growth.” Krishnavallabh Swami asked, “But if you had not travelled extensively and made such great efforts, how could all of this have happened?” Swamishri repeated the same idea, “Yogiji Maharaj had wished for an increase in Satsang, and that is why we had to travel and make efforts.”Swamishri’s humility, guru bhakti and detachment from all his accomplishments is simply amazing!

Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the abhishek mandap. Devotees fit to be introduced and devotees from out of town were sitting here. After darshan of the abhishek, Swamishri moved forward, meeting all these devotees. Shashikantbhai Bhojani, Joint MD of ICICI Bank, was sitting right in front. Tirthswarup Swami was introducing him, but Swamishri's attention was on Govindbhai Fojdar, sitting right at the back, and so Swamishri was blessing him with gestures and casting his glance on him. Only after Govindbhai was satisfied did Swamishri cast his glance on Shashikantbhai.

ds.t: If I cough, I'll drink water and carry on
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj's health is getting better. Swamishri himself had expressed the wish to go to the Sunday assembly, and today was the first day. In this context, during his walk, Dr Kiranbhai Doshi said, "Today you will be going to the Sunday assembly for the first time, so when you give blessings, do not speak for more than ten minutes; you will start coughing."
Swamishri said simply, laughing, "If I start coughing, I will drink water and start again."
What enthusiasm Swamishri has at the age of 90!!
Today during the midday meal, a flow of memories of Mahant Swami Maharaj's stay in Mumbai began.

Dharmasutdas Swami, a direct witness of those memories, said, "Mahant Swami Maharaj lived in the room for mattresses and quilts. In it lay the sadhus' store, along with stoves, coal, sacking and everything. Behind, the grinding mill and the pump would be running all the time! In there Swamishri would sit on an aluminium chair with a quilt thrown over it. He slept on top of the pile of mattresses. The path to get there was such that two people could not pass each other."
"So how did you climb on top of that pile?" the sadhus asked Swamishri himself.
"By putting my feet between the mattresses and going up..." Swamishri said.
At this point Atmaswarupdas Swami added, "Many people used the mattress spread out for Swamishri as a pillow."
Hearing this, Swamishri smiled in agreement and said, "Everyone." Then, explaining with a gesture of his hand, he said, "Like the rays of the sun (everyone would arrange themselves)..."

This natural conversation then turned to the Sunday assemblies of that time. In this Swamishri remembered an incident. So, with a gentle smile, he said, "Once I had a fever. So I did not go to the Sunday assembly. I was lying in my room. Then after the assembly, 200 people came one after another down that lane to see me. I thought, 'It would have been better to have just gone to the assembly once!'"

After that the sadhus described the seating arrangement of that time: "A cushion and a bolster were placed for you. A cushion for Kotharibapa, and a rug was spread for all the others." Having said this, they added, "If you did not have a bolster, Yogibapa would ask, 'Why does Mahant Swami not have a bolster?'"
Hearing this, Swamishri laughed openly and said, "I still don't feel that I am Mahant."
"You have not let us feel it either!" Adarshjivandas Swami said.
Then Swamishri said, "There is no fun in that (in standing apart). The fun is when we all mix together." Then he said, "From the very start, firm love for the Satpurush, nothing else."
So the conversation took many turns, but they were joyful and, even more, full of memories. With every word of it, Swamishri's personality kept unfolding.

Today, while Mahant Swami Maharaj was having his meal, Gunvatsaldas Swami suspected that the parval (pointed gourd) tasted bitter. Munichintandas Swami tasted it and it really was bitter. When Swamishri was asked, Swamishri too said yes. The attendants asked, "Then why didn't you say anything? You ate three such bitter parvals."
Hiding his own virtue, Swamishri said, "I ate the first, then I thought the second would not be bitter, and then the third..."
Everyone had darshan of Swamishri's freedom from attachment to taste.

Munichintandas Swami recalled another incident: "On the way to Surendranagar, devotees had offered dry fruit to Harikrishna Maharaj. From it we insisted and fed you a pecan, a dry fruit like a red walnut, and then when we took some ourselves we found that it was very rancid. Bad enough to make your hair fall out! Even then you did not say a single word, nor did a line of your face change."

Now, this is the very limit of freedom from attachment to taste. Perhaps someone might not say anything, but the expressions and lines of the face would certainly change. But this is the Gunatit Satpurush, his ways are altogether different.
